pure-announcement.rationale: It is the full text of an IETF Standards Track specification, not a launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: MCP authorization hardening cites RFC 9207 iss validation as a requirement but does not teach the mechanism — a reader of that concept still learns the mix-up attack mechanics, the exact validation procedure, and why response integrity protection is unnecessary from this source.

unfalsifiable.rationale: It is a normative primary source whose central claim — iss checking defeats mix-up attacks — is backed by a cited formal security analysis.

durability.rationale: A Standards Track countermeasure stable since 2022, formally proven effective, and now being made mandatory downstream (e.g. by MCP), so it will hold well beyond twelve months.

actionability.rationale: It gives exact MUST-level behaviour for both sides — servers include iss and advertise support in metadata; clients decode, string-compare against the expected issuer, reject mismatches, and track per-server support in mixed deployments.

atomicity.rationale: The whole document is one idea — a single response parameter countering a single attack class — statable in one paragraph.
